expectations.name: production-rules-while-writing
expected_behavior: Applies the Production section: gofmt and goimports, lines within the line limit it resolved for the module, `%w` error wrapping with short context, godoc on exported symbols
Applies no Test-only rule to the production file — no `have`/`want` naming, no subtest conventions

expectations.name: test-rules-inherit-production
expected_behavior: Applies the Test section on top of Production, not instead of it
Names tests `Test_Func` / `Test_Type_Method`, suffixes the table test `_tabular`, and uses `t.Run` subtests
Calls `t.Helper()` in helpers and reaches for `tester.Spy` when testing a helper
Keeps subtest names inside the `[a-zA-Z0-9 _-]` charset, flat, with no `/`

expectations.name: pass-lists-offenses-then-asks
expected_behavior: Resolves the target, the line limit and tab width, and lists the files in scope on the report's first line; reads `references/checking.md`
Reasons only for detection — runs no gofmt, vet, or linter
Opens only the `rules.md` entries for the rules it flags — the file is never read whole, which is visible in the commands the run issued.
Reports style offenses only: the off-by-one is left to `go:review`, not reported here
Groups findings Blocker / Should-fix / Nit with `file:line`, the rule id, and a minimal fix; ends with a clean / fix-first verdict and per-severity counts
Asks which offenses to apply rather than editing unprompted

expectations.name: fix-applies-everything-behind-a-green-gate
expected_behavior: Runs `go test ./... -race` for a green baseline before editing anything
Applies every listed fix, then re-runs the gate
Reports each fix as one `file:sym — what changed` line plus the gate result
Prints no diffs and never commits

expectations.name: delegated-by-review
expected_behavior: Runs the pass through the offense list and stops — no pick step and no edits
Returns the grouped offense list for `review` to merge with its correctness findings

expectations.name: rules-change-only-through-review
expected_behavior: Routes the request to `go:review` rule-edit mode instead of hand-editing `SKILL.md` or `rules.md`
The redirect names the rule-edit command to run (`/review add …`) with the user's rule carried in it, and `style` writes nothing itself — `SKILL.md`, `rules.md`, and every other file stay unchanged

expectations.name: broad-target-auto-plan-first
expected_behavior: Switches to plan-first on its own: the target is broad and the invocation carries no budget, so it proposes rather than checking
The proposal names the `max_issues` and `depth` defaults it would use and the packages in scope
Stops there and waits: no package is checked, no offense list or finding is presented alongside the proposal, no file is edited — plan-first is propose-then-stop, not check-everything-then-present

expectations.name: terse-output
expected_behavior: Opens with the target/file-set line and then the offenses — that line is the first fact, not preamble
No narration of reading the rules, and no restating of the invocation
States each offense once
No closing summary re-listing offenses the user can already see

expectations.name: incidental-interface-satisfaction
expected_behavior: Flags `(*Conn).Close`, whose assertion declares it is written to the interface
Leaves `(*Buffer).Close` alone: incidentally matching an interface is not writing to one, and `goToImplementation` matching is not the test
Does not strip godoc from ordinary `Close`/`String`/`Error` methods on the strength of a signature match

expectations.name: severity-and-ids-are-stable
expected_behavior: Gives the same offense the same severity in all three packages
Gives the same offense the same rule id in all three packages — the `rules.md` key, never a coined one
Puts the missing exported godoc at Blocker and the receiver naming at Should-fix, per the rubric

expectations.name: fanout-folds-then-caps
expected_behavior: Does not stop for a plan: the invocation already carries `max_issues=N`, so the budget needs no proposing and the run proceeds to check
Fans out one subagent per package, each checking the same pinned rule set
Gives workers no share of `max_issues` — they report everything and the cap applies once at the merge
Folds by rule id before cutting: the godoc rule broken in all eight packages is one finding listing eight, not eight findings
Cuts nothing: the ten folded findings fit under the cap of 25, so the report carries all ten and says no offense went unreported — a cap applied before folding would have dropped 13 of the 38

The merged report carries each rule under exactly one id and one severity across all eight packages — no rule appearing in two spellings or two tiers, and no note reconciling id or severity spellings at the end

Reports the raw total as the sum of the worker reports plus any adjustment the merge made, each adjustment itemised — add the eight figures and the itemised adjustments up and the reported total equals them, rather than being carried from the plan or from the planted count
Still runs the pick step: a budget supplied on the invocation agreed the budget, not the fixes, so the run asks which offenses to apply and edits no file until told which

Derives ids by the documented steps: the four rules broken in every package come back as `wrap-errors-w`, `receivers-three-letter-type`, `every-exported-symbol`, and `separate-distinct-topics`; a negation survives (`No work in init()` gives `no-work-init`, never `work-init`); a dotted identifier contributes only the part before its dot

The final report grades identical code identically: across the packages that differ only in their package name, every rule it reports on one it reports on all, with no rule reported in a minority of them — the missing blank line between two `--- Given ---` topic groups among them. Graded on the report the user sees, not on the worker reports

Resolves a split before reporting it: every rule flagged in some packages but not all — including the six offenses each held by a single package — gets a re-check of the packages that did not flag it, shown (what it searched for and what it found) in the reply or in a file it saved before the reply, and the report carries the reconciled count rather than the raw spread. FAIL when no such re-check is shown
No folded finding prescribes inserting what another of its own sites prescribes deleting
Flags no blank-line offense for an `assert.NoError` sitting next to the `assert.Equal` that checks the same call's result: one `--- When ---` call's returns are one subject
Every offense quotes the source text that triggered it, so a reader can tell a located offense from a pattern-matched one

expectations.name: fanout-opposing-fixes-kept-apart
expected_behavior: Fans out one subagent per package — eight — each checking the same pinned rule set
Reports the blank-line topic rule as one finding under one id and one severity, listing all eight packages

Keeps each site's own fix: the four packages missing a blank line get an `insert`, the four with a surplus one get a `delete` — no site's fix replaced by the majority's or by one prescription for all eight
Shows a re-check of the opposing sites against the source — what it searched for and what it found — in the reply or in a file it saved before the reply, before the report
Flags no offense at the correct blank line before the second action in `--- Then ---` present in every package
Every fix opens with its verb, so the direction at each site reads without parsing prose
Edits no file before the pick step; if fixes are picked, the four missing packages gain exactly one blank line and the four surplus packages lose exactly one, and nothing else in any file changes
